title: OpenAI Q3 Revenue Surges to $10 Billion: Up Nearly 50% Quarter-over-Quarter, Enterprise Business Doubles in a Single Quarter

content_html:
OpenAI's pace of commercial monetization is reshaping outside perceptions of the AI industry. On Tuesday, U.S. Eastern Time, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar disclosed the company's latest financial and business data in a media interview. The data shows that in the just-ended third quarter, OpenAI's quarterly revenue grew nearly 50% quarter over quarter in an explosive surge, reaching $10 billion, while its equivalent annualized revenue has climbed to about $50 billion, with unusually rapid growth momentum.

Core Growth Engine: Enterprise Business Doubles QoQ, Now on Par with Consumer Business

Looking back at this year's second quarter, OpenAI's revenue grew about 18% quarter over quarter, while the nearly 50% jump in the third quarter broke its previous growth pace. Friar pointed out that the core drivers of this impressive growth were mainly the rapid development of frontier models and the full-scale breakout of its enterprise business.

In terms of revenue mix, OpenAI's enterprise business and consumer business are now evenly split, each accounting for about half. Among them, "our enterprise business revenue doubled quarter over quarter," Friar emphasized in the interview. This standout performance was mainly driven by faster deployment of innovations such as code-generation tools, cybersecurity products, and Dots, an AI agent platform launched for enterprises. In addition, the small and medium-sized business (SMB) market also performed strongly in the third quarter, with growth exceeding the combined total of the previous six quarters.

On the consumer side, overall sales rose 20% quarter over quarter, paying subscribers officially surpassed the 100 million mark, and total weekly active users reached 1.2 billion. Its massive user base continues to expand steadily.

Competitive Landscape and Future Plans: Benchmarking a Peer's Ecosystem and Reassessing Cloud Partnerships

It is worth noting that around the same time OpenAI disclosed its strong earnings, its main competitor Anthropic also officially launched its IPO roadshow and plans to list on U.S. stock markets next week. Relevant financial data shows that Anthropic's revenue soared in the first nine months of this year, and its business model is focused entirely on the enterprise market, with no consumer-facing business.

Anthropic's strong performance in the enterprise market also gave OpenAI management a different perspective on growth. Friar acknowledged that the rival's success in the enterprise market made her realize that OpenAI needs to focus on signing distribution partnership agreements with more third-party cloud providers in the future. She explained that the company's distribution had previously been largely constrained by its exclusive or close contract with Microsoft Azure, and after seeing the diversity of the industry ecosystem, opening up third-party cloud distribution channels will become an important growth driver for the company in 2027.
